messages:
mia: heads-up, bringing archipelago14b-int6 canary up. quick eval shows a math QA exact-match drop vs fp32 baseline (~82% -> 76%). posting samples.
raj: link to the eval run id?
mia: eval id eval-arch-6181. command and short output:
```
./eval.sh --model archipelago14b-int6 --suite mathqa --split test --run-id eval-arch-6181
Total examples: 1200
ExactMatch: 76.1
Baseline(fp32): 82.4
Latency p50: 110ms (fp32 120ms)
No OOMs, no crashes.
```
oliver: interesting — latency ✅, stability ✅, but quality down. is this purely quant noise or a tokenizer/precision combo? :thinking:
mia: errors cluster on fraction/ratio arithmetic and multi-step simplifications. examples:
- prompt: "Compute 3/7 + 5/14"
  int6: "0.428..." (wrong)
  fp32: "0.714..." (correct)
- prompt: "What is 7/8 - 1/16?" -> off-by-factor in int6 outputs.

eva: could be quantization of small-weight magnitudes hurting normalization layers. can you dump logits/top tokens for failing cases?
raj: two quick probes:
1) eval with layer-protect (first 2 layers fp16) to see if head layers are sensitive
2) run quant-calib with kl+tiny-mse loss (we did only symmetric-min in the onboarding)

oliver: i'll stand up an A/B: route 10% traffic to int6 with layer-protect=first2 and collect traces. infra-bot will create the canary.
infra-bot: canary deploy initiated: canary-arch-6181 -> nodes [gpu-a2-11,gpu-a3-04], routing 10% traffic, trace sampling=1% :rocket:

mia: i attached a tiny repro snippet (ran locally on dev box):
```
>>> from rl_eval import run_one
>>> run_one("Compute 3/7 + 5/14", model="archipelago14b-int6")
{"tokens": [...], "logits_top": [[...]], "answer": "0.428..."}
```
raj: also check tokenizer alignment and prompt normalization. on some models token boundaries cause numerical tokens to be represented oddly and quant amplifies it.
eva: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback to fp32 for mathqa route (painful)
- layer-protect canary (cheap, try first)
- re-run quant calibration with a targeted math/rational prompt set
- as a temporary config, reduce default max_new_tokens from 128 -> 64 for the canary to shrink accumulation windows (not a fix but lessens long-step error surface)

oliver: plan agreed: (1) layer-protect canary (2) targeted quant-cal with kl+mse on math prompts (3) run focused eval and attach failing traces. if still bad after 24h -> rollback.
mia: i'll run the targeted eval now (kicked off eval-arch-6181b) and post results here. thanks :eyes:
raj: add an eval metric for 'rational-precision' (exact-match on fraction simplification) so we can gate future onboardings.
mia: ack. also logging note: saw a kernel fallback in the canary logs once — posting snippet:
```
[2026-03-23T14:02:12Z] WARN kernel-selector: fallback to matmul-small-kernel for layer 8 due to int6 alignment
```
raj: that kernel mismatch could explain per-layer sensitivity. oliver, can infra pin kernel-version on the canary nodes?
oliver: yes, will pin and re-run traces. infra-bot: pinned kernel image gpu-a2-11 -> cudakernel-v3.4 for canary.
infra-bot: pin applied :white_check_mark:
mia: thanks all — will update with eval-arch-6181b results in ~30m. if anyone wants samples, ping me.
